name: City Council Regular Meeting of March 12, 2025

APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF MARCH 12, 2025

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:01 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Marisol Cortez, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Sheila Crippen-Thomas, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Cindy Galvan, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Martin Herrera, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Viviana Longoria, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Dr. Julia Ruedas, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Councilmember Dr. Ruedas
  s) Councilmember Galvan  7-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various legislative bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council will attempt to address and complete
  all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. If the City Council
  completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the City Council will take a short
  recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m. In the event
  the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed Session items by
  7:00 p.m., the City Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the
  meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of the
  public wish to address the City Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the City
  Council shall allow such person to address the City Council on such matter(s) prior to
  going into Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall (i) call-in or submit a speaker card in the manner
  prescribed on page 1 of this agenda, above, prior to the City Council going into closed
  session; and (ii) be subject to a single speaker time allotment of three (3) continuous
  minutes total per speaker to address the City Council on any or all closed session items
  of business.

  Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
  Session Items 4.1 through 4.3. Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into
  Closed Session at approximately 6:02 p.m.

  At 7:00 p.m. the City Clerk announced that the City Council would reconvene at 7:15
  p.m.

  Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:18 p.m.

  4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation – Leos vs. City of El Monte,
  Central District Court Case No. 2:23-cv-02427.

  City Council received an update from legal counsel, feedback given, but no
  final action taken.
   City Council Meeting Minutes of March 12, 2025

  4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation – One (1) Matter.

  City Council received an update from legal counsel, feedback given, but no
  final action taken.

  4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference with
  Labor Negotiators.

  Bargaining Units Subject to Negotiations: El Monte General Unit (SEIU Local
  721); El Monte General Mid-Management Unit (SEIU Local 721); El Monte Police
  Officers Association; and El Monte Police Mid-Manager’s Association.

  City’s Designated Negotiator: Alma Martinez, City Manager; and Rigoberto
  Gutierrez, Human Resources/Risk Management Director.

  City Council received an update from legal counsel, feedback given, but no
  final action taken.

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

(Commencing at 7:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
Session/Short Recess).

5.  INVOCATION:  Chaplain. Chaplain Manny Coronilla.

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  Sophia Gomez, 6th Grade Student from Twin Lakes School.
  Present

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS:

  7.1  Presentation by the City Council to Sophia Gomez from Twin Lakes School for
  Leading the Pledge of Allegiance. Present

  7.2  Presentation by the City Council to Our Local Businesses in Appreciation for Their
  Donations to the Eaton Fire Victims. Present

8.  GENERAL PUBLIC COMMENT:

  This time has been set aside for members of the public to directly address the City Council
  on agendized items of business (other than those agendized as public hearing or closed
  session items) or on any other matter of interest to the speaker/caller that is within the
  subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing Authority, the Financing
  Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”). Each speaker/caller will
  be limited to a single allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total to address the Council
  on any or all matters covered by this section. As explained more specifically under the
  Public Hearing portion of this agenda, members of the public wishing to offer comment on
  items of business agendized under the Public Hearing portion of the agenda shall have a
  separate allotment of three (3) continuous minutes per speaker per public hearing item.
  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration
  at a future meeting. Persons wishing to address the Council on matters covered under
  General Public Comment shall call in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed
  on page 1 of this agenda, above, by or before the General Public Comment portion of the
  agenda is closed. The City Council shall be under no obligation to entertain comments
  from speakers/callers who submit cards or call in to speak on matters covered by the
  section after the General Public Comment portion of the agenda is closed.

  2
   City Council Meeting Minutes of March 12, 2025

  Kelly Hadnott-Brown – PIO for the Office of Disaster Recover & Resilience. Provided

  Rachel Lizotte – Provided updates for Norwood Library.

9.  CITY TREASURER’S REPORT: None

10.  DEMAND RESOLUTION NO. D-726

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA,
  ALLOWING CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT
  OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID.

  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA, DOES RESOLVE AS
  FOLLOWS: SECTION 1. That the attached list of claims and demands totaling
  $7,887,133.08 have been examined by the City Treasurer and that warrant numbers
  1129051 through 1129290, and the payroll period February 1, 2025 through February 15,
  2025 inclusive are hereby allowed in the amounts and ordered paid out of the respective
  funds as set forth.

  m) Councilmember Galvan
  s) Councilmember Crippen-Thomas  7-0

11.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES: None

12.  CONSENT CALENDAR:

  All matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine in nature and
  may be enacted by one motion approving the recommendation listed on the Agenda. One
  or more items may be removed from the Consent Calendar so that they may be discussed,
  considered, and voted upon individually by the Council. A matter may be removed from
  the Consent Calendar and taken up separately by way of a seconded motion of any
  member of the Council with the approval of a majority of the Council quorum.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

13.  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

  Members of the public wishing to address the Council on any item of business agendized
  under this Public Hearing portion of the agenda are asked to submit a speaker card for
  each Public Hearing item of business they wish to address the Council on. Each speaker
  will be allotted three (3) continuous minutes per Public Hearing item. Members of the
  public are asked to submit speaker cards to the City Clerk or the Sergeant-of-Arms before
  the Council’s approval of the agenda, if possible. The Council is under no obligation to
  recognize a speaker who submits a speaker card for a particular Public Hearing item of
  business after the public comment portion of the public hearing for that item has closed.

  [No Public Hearing Items Agendized for this Council meeting]

   City Council Meeting Minutes of March 12, 2025

  14.3  Consideration and Approval of a Resolution Setting the Date, Time, and Place of
  a Majority-Protest Public Hearing Per Article XIIID, Section 6 of the California
  Constitution and Government Code Section 53755 Et Seq. to Receive Written
  Protests by Affected Real Property Parcel Owners to Proposed Increases to the
  City’s Schedule of Sewer Service Fees and Charges; Approving a Master List of
  Affected Parcels; Approving a Related Sewer Service Charge Rate Study;
  Approving Rules for the Submission and Tabulation of Written Protests; and
  Directing Staff to Undertake all Other Measures Required to Conduct a Majority-
  Protest Hearing.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BU SINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Receive the presentation from City staff and Raftelis regarding the preparation
  of the 2025 Sewer Rate Study supporting the proposed approval of a schedule
  of increase sewer service fees and charges and pose questions to staff; and
  2. Approve the attached Resolution which:
   Sets the date, time and location of a majority-protest public hearing;
   Approves the master list of affected real property parcels;
   Accepts the Raftelis 2025 Sewer Rate Study and adopt its findings and
  proposed schedule of increased sewer service fees and charges;
   Approves rules and procedures for the submission of written protests;
   Directs City staff to undertake all other procedures required by law,
  including the issuance of 45-day notices to affected property owners.
  Total Cost: N/A  Account No:  N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  Resolution No. 10591

15.  CITY ATTORNEY’S AGENDA:

16.  CITY MANAGER’S AGENDA:

  16.1  Update Regarding Traffic Enforcement from the Police Department.

  Chief Fisher provided the City Council with overview update on crime, activity and
  traffic issues.

  Mayor Ancona wanted to confirm that this is compared to the same two (2) months
  from last year.

  Councilmember Crippen-Thomas asked what to do with the automatic bikes with
  no lights zooming through the streets.

  Chief Fisher advised that if residents see this going on they can call the Police
  Department to report this.

  Mayor Pro Tem Cortez thanked the Chief for the presentation and said this was
  good information. Also spoke about the automatic bikes/scooters.

  Councilmember Herrera thanked the Chief for the presentation. Also spoke about
  the automatic bikes and indicated that it is not only kids using these. Also spoke
  about the vendor food court on the state highway property.

  Chief Fisher will partner with Economic Development Director Steve Fowler to
  brainstorm on how to address this matter.

  Mayor Ancona asked which agency Highway Patrol or Sheriffs.

  6
   City Council Meeting Minutes of March 12, 2025

  Councilmember Longoria thanked the Chief for addressing the concerns she had.
  Thanked the Police Department for addressing the issue at Tito’s Plaza.

  Chief Fisher appreciates the returned reciprocated survey that callers get to let the
  Police Department know how they are doing.

  16.2  Update Regarding Crime Stats from the Police Department.

17.  WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS:

18.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPORTS:

  18A.  Mayor Ancona

  Mayor Ancona spoke about Assembly Bill 259. The Mayor of Azusa reached out
  and inquired if the City of El Monte would support this Assembly Bill relating to
  remote participation in meetings.

  Mayor Pro Tem Cortez asked what past practice is regarding a request like this.

  City Attorney Olivarez advised the City Council there is no prescribed process or
  procedure, the Council could give direction to the Mayor advising that they are
  supporting this.

  Mayor Ancona said there is a draft letter that the City Council could use and send
  to show support.

  Councilmember Herrera asked about the process. Council may have additional
  questions and do their own research.

  City Attorney Olivarez informed the City Council that they can bring back.

  Mayor Ancona asked to bring back in two (2) weeks.

  Councilmember Dr. Ruedas asked about the process too. What has been the
  process for items like this.

  18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Cortez

  Expressed her appreciation for Sunday’s event, the Be Nutritous re-grand opening.
  Thanked Economic Development and Publics Works.

  Mayor Ancona mentioned there is a lot to celebrate in the city of El Monte. Had a
  grand opening of US Bank, re-grand opening of Be Nutritious, Little League Open
  Day coming back.  Invited everyone this Saturday to the Zamora Park
  Groundbreaking Ceremony at 11:00 am.

  18C.  Councilwoman Crippen-Thomas

  18C.1 Thank you to Residents for Attending the Community Meeting – District 1
  Held on Thursday, February 27, 2025, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at
  Cherrylee Elementary School Located at 5025 Buffington Road, El Monte,
  CA 91732.

  Councilmember Crippen-Thomas thanked the residents for attending the
  community meeting. Thanked her colleagues for being there to support.

  18C.2 Invitation to the El Monte Historical Museum Open House March 16, 2025,
  from 1:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. at 3150 Tyler Avenue, El Monte.

  Councilmember Crippen-Thomas invited everyone to Museum’s Open
  House. Spoke about two (2) new items the museum just received.

  18D.  Councilwoman Galvan

  18E.  Councilman Herrera

  18F.  Councilwoman Longoria

  Adjourn the meeting

  The next Regular Meeting of the City Council will be held on March 26, 2025 at 6:00 p.m.

  posted no less than 72 hours prior to the start of the subject regular meeting. Although it

  supporting material as part of its website posting, the size or formatting of certain
  supporting materials may render their website posting infeasible. Nevertheless, all

  members of the council may be inspected by members of the public at the City Clerk’s
  Office located at 11333 Valley Boulevard, El Monte, Monday through Thursday, 7:00 am
  – 5:30 pm. For more information, please call the City Clerk’s Office at 626-580-2016.

  All public meetings and events sponsored or conducted by the City of El Monte are held
  in sites accessible to persons with disabilities. Requests for accommodations may be
